newsitem.title: USA: DA to drop charges vs. Orange Cty official-sources.
newsitem.headline: DA to drop charges vs. Orange Cty official-sources.

text.p: The Orange County, Calif., District Attorney on Monday will drop felony charges against former county Budget Director Ronald Rubino, people involved in the negotiations said Friday.
In exchange, Rubino will enter a no contest plea at a hearing to a new charge brought by the District Attorney. That charge will be treated as a misdemeanor, the sources said.
The misdemeanor will allege a record-keeping violation.
In pleading no contest to the single misdemeanor, Rubino will agree to 100 hours of community service and to two years of unsupervised probation.

At the end of the first year of probation, Rubino will petition the court to withdraw his no contest plea to the misdemeanor, will have a not guilty plea entered, and will have the misdemeanor charge dismissed, sources said.
An attorney for Rubino declined to comment on the deal pending a hearing Monday in Santa Ana. Officials in the District Attorney's office were not immediately available to comment.
Rubino, 44, was indicted by a county grand jury in December 1995 for allegedly aiding former county Treasurer Robert Citron in diverting funds from other government agencies for the county's benefit.
Rubino has denied any wrongdoing. The maximum punishment for the felony charges was nine years in state prison.
Rubino's trial, the first criminal trial arising from the Orange County bankruptcy, began in August, but ended in a mistrial on September 13.
A new trial for Rubino was set to begin next week.
Orange County filed for protection under Chapter 9 of the federal Bankruptcy Code on Dec 6, 1994, after sustaining investment losses of more than $1.6 billion.
The county emerged from bankruptcy in June of this year.
